title: Role-factored relation encoder with joint future-geometry diffusion
coverage_gap: Two successful LL/HH trajectories confound absolute positions and provide little variation in grip failures or independent nut/peg placement. Action imitation alone may encode hand motion while neglecting whether the eccentric ring actually follows the hand and aligns with the peg.
reusable_regularity: Represent four typed relations with a shared learned edge encoder: hand-to-handle acquisition, ring-to-handle rigid link, ring-to-peg alignment, and hand-to-peg proximity. Mix the ordered relation embeddings and retain a physical skip path. Jointly denoise actions and future ring-goal / handle-hand / aperture trajectories so the common temporal U-Net is trained to associate commanded motion with the object's relative evolution. This tests learned relational dynamics without prescribing phase thresholds or rotating actions.
dependencies_preserved: The handle and ring are distinct nodes. The ring-to-handle edge and sign-invariant body orientation columns preserve eccentricity and tilt; hand-to-handle is not substituted for ring-to-peg alignment.

Signed world-axis edge vectors and a world hand anchor make every current node position reconstructible in the deterministic skip path, preventing a learned bottleneck from deleting necessary absolute reach information.
All four heights, the hand-to-peg edge and ring-to-peg edge preserve table/gravity, clearance and peg obstacle dependencies. The fixed native gripper and world-action axes are retained.

Shared raw two-observation history, native previous translational/aperture fields, measured hand/site/ring displacements and body axes allow the network to infer binding and motion. No time index or phase oracle is supplied.
Absent object2 fields and redundant native-previous quaternion are omitted. No simulator, collision model, reset factors, reward, success rules or test-time targets are accessed.

evidence_refs.detail: Exact D_N is the two assembly support episodes listed here; all future training labels will come from these episodes only
Common runtime hand, handle site, body quaternion, ring center and peg goal fields; two-row history and native world action4; independent development layout factors
Only 179 transitions across one LL and one HH episode; substantial hand/ring height change and a small set of observed grip apertures

obs 0:3 distinguishes ring and handle by approximately 0.13 m in x; obs 22:28 is nearly stationary ring during descent, while obs 46:51 and 72:76 show carried ring/site motion. actions 0:40 and 42:87 expose different lift/transport/descent commands
obs 50:53 confirms the coupled handle/hand and ring evolution during second-episode carrying; actions 47:55 change lateral sign relative to demo_00
Ring, handle, hand and peg form distinct physical roles
Acquisition happens at the offset handle, supporting a separate grasp relation
Ring and grasped handle lift together
Carrier motion has brought the ring toward peg alignment
The final physical relation is ring over peg, not hand over peg

expected_failure_signature: Joint diffusion can hallucinate successful future ring motion after a weak or missed grasp; the observable failure would be hand transport with a stationary or dropped ring despite learned geometry predictions.

A learned relation mixer may still overfit two layouts. If passive relative-coordinate models outperform this one on opposite-sign cells, the extra learned factorization/auxiliary task did not resolve the coverage gap.
Future-geometry channels may distract from sharp action switches at closure or descent; failures should appear as smeared phase transitions or hovering even when the correct geometry is observed.

No counterfactual physics is supplied. At far extrapolation, generated state and action trajectories may be mutually plausible under D_N but physically inconsistent under new reach and saturation demands.

required_runtime_fields.source: condition reads only causal_context.raw_history [B,2,42]; denoise reads only the common noisy joint sample, diffusion timestep and causal conditioning
required_runtime_fields.representation: Each of four edges has 21 inputs: signed displacement3, 3D range1, planar range1, source/target heights2, relative measured displacement3, role one-hot4, body axes6 and aperture1. Shared 21->64->24 SiLU encoder; concatenate four edge embeddings, mix 96->96->64. Append 36 direct physical features to yield [B,2,100]. Ring displacement is zero for the earlier history row and the observed two-row difference for the later row.
required_runtime_fields.action_frame: The first four diffusion channels are unchanged native world_dx, world_dy, world_dz and gripper. Identity encode/decode, native 0.01 m xyz scale, fixed end-effector orientation and untouched gripper semantics. Only the host clips the decoded native cube and executes its fixed prefix.
required_runtime_fields.inference_auxiliaries: Seven additional joint channels start as host-owned diffusion noise and are denoised jointly. They are generated internal outputs, discarded by the executor, never future ground-truth conditioning and never used for rollout, search or planning.

training_only_targets.name: future_relations
training_only_targets.source: For each support episode and chunk start t, valid action k is paired with obs[t+k+1]. Channels 0:3=(future ring_center_xyz - obs[t,36:39])/0.1; 3:6=(future handle_site_xyz - future hand_xyz)/0.1; 6=2*(future gripper-0.5). This includes the final obs[T] only as a training target, not as normalization or deployment input.
training_only_targets.padding: Zero after the last real action; no labels from outside the episode. No target tensor or support episode is retained on the deployed module.
training_only_targets.joint_mapping: diffusion_targets concatenates encoded native action4 first, then these seven targets, yielding action_dim=11.
training_only_targets.loss: Additional nonnegative epsilon MSE over channels 4:11 only, normalized by mask.sum()*7 (clamped to one only for the all-invalid case), weight 0.2. Uses the common valid-action mask. The public action epsilon loss stays weight 1 with its own mask.sum()*4 denominator.

support_fit: None; no fitted statistics, pretrained weights, extra demonstrations or cached trajectories. Physical feature and target scales are fixed constants. The common support normalizer is left unchanged.
architecture: One unmodified common DP factory call, condition_dim=100 and diffusion_action_dim=11. All extra learned layers are registered during build_modules and receive gradients through joint action/auxiliary loss. No auxiliary controller, alternate optimizer, U-Net edits or additional updates.
change_summary: Initial independent scientific design: learned shared role-relation encoding plus joint future-geometry denoising, using identity world action encoding and no prescribed soft stages. No development scores or performance-driven edits.
